surfaces.label: Clay - smooth / groomed
surfaces.note: Watered and groomed indoor clay; very high, consistent grip that blue-grooves along the racing line.

surfaces.label: Clay - dry / dusty
surfaces.note: Clay that has dried out; a dust film cuts side-bite and makes grip line-dependent.

surfaces.label: Hard-packed dirt
surfaces.note: Compacted abrasive dirt; high grip but eats pins, favors long-wear compounds and low-profile treads.

surfaces.label: Blue groove (rubbered hard pack)
surfaces.note: Rubber laid into hard pack forms a dark groove; huge grip on line, slick off line.

surfaces.label: Dusty blue groove
surfaces.note: Blue groove with loose dust on top; grip improves as the line cleans, very inconsistent early in the day.

surfaces.label: Loose dirt / loam
surfaces.note: Fresh, moist loamy soil; moderate diggy grip, full-pin tires bite well, surface evolves fast.

surfaces.label: Sugar / fluffy dirt
surfaces.note: Dry powdery 'sugar' surface; very low grip, polishes tires, soft compounds and big pins needed.

surfaces.label: Grass
surfaces.note: Slippery with high rolling resistance; full spikes work best, grip drops sharply when wet.

surfaces.label: Astroturf (artificial turf)
surfaces.note: UK/EU-style astro; consistent medium-high grip, abrasive on pins, low-profile mini-pin territory.

surfaces.label: Carpet offroad (EOS style)
surfaces.note: Indoor needle-pile race carpet; extreme consistent grip, traction-rolling risk, hard mini-pin or slick tires.

surfaces.label: Mixed astro + dirt
surfaces.note: UK-style mixed sections of turf and dirt; compromise tire and setup between both surfaces.

surfaces.label: Wood / plywood sections
surfaces.note: Wood ramps and flooring sections on indoor tracks; low slippery grip, sensitive to dust.

surfaces.label: Sand
surfaces.note: Very low grip, car digs in; paddle or full-spike tires, grip improves slightly when damp.

surfaces.label: Gravel
surfaces.note: Loose stones over base; low unpredictable grip (rally-style), harsh on tires and drivetrain.

surfaces.label: Mud / wet dirt
surfaces.note: Wet sticky soil that clogs treads; open full-pin or cut-stagger treads to self-clean.

surfaces.label: Snow
surfaces.note: Very low grip and cold tires; spikes or paddles, compounds stay too hard in cold.

surfaces.label: Ice
surfaces.note: Minimal grip; studded or pin tires required, throttle and steering inputs must be tiny.

surfaces.label: Asphalt - low grip (green/dusty)
surfaces.note: Unrubbered or dusty asphalt (parking lot); low traction, softer compounds and additive needed.

surfaces.label: Asphalt - high grip (rubbered/treated)
surfaces.note: Rubbered-in or sugar/traction-treated race asphalt; very high grip, harder compounds, traction-roll watch.

surfaces.label: Tarmac street circuit
surfaces.note: Public-road tarmac; variable bumpy grip with dust and crowning, durability matters.

surfaces.label: Carpet onroad (ETS/CRC)
surfaces.note: ETS-style black carpet or CRC ozite; extreme consistent grip, dedicated carpet compounds (e.g. 28 shore) and stiff sidewalls.

surfaces.label: Painted / sealed concrete
surfaces.note: Paint-sealed concrete; medium grip that builds with rubber, slippery when cold or dusty.

surfaces.label: Polished concrete
surfaces.note: Smooth polished slab; low-to-medium grip, very sensitive to dust and tire additive.

surfaces.label: Rough concrete (unpainted)
surfaces.note: Bare rough concrete; medium grip but very abrasive, accelerated tire wear.

surfaces.label: RCP foam tile (mini scale)
surfaces.note: Interlocking foam tile (Mini-Z/RCP); moderate predictable grip for small scales, wears in over time.

surfaces.label: Hard-packed abrasive clay
surfaces.note: Compacted clay with a gritty, sandpaper-like crust that chews tires; medium grip but high-wear, favours harder compounds and short pins.

surfaces.label: Loamy clay (soil over clay base)
surfaces.note: Loose loamy top over a firmer clay base; common outdoor club mix that runs loose early then grooves up, line-dependent grip.

surfaces.label: Watered / tacky clay
surfaces.note: Clay/loam watered to raise traction and kill dust; high, tacky bite — the qualifying condition on dirt and clay ovals.

surfaces.label: Deep sand
surfaces.note: Beach/dune-style deep loose sand; very low grip, needs aggressive long-pin or paddle tires on buggy/truggy and rally-raid rigs.

surfaces.label: Decomposed granite / DG
surfaces.note: Crushed-granite (DG) tracks common in the US Southwest; hard, dusty and gritty, watered to tack up — low-to-medium grip.

surfaces.label: Off-road carpet (low-grip / worn)
surfaces.note: Older/worn or short-pile club off-road carpet; less bite than EOS high-pile, changes ideal spike length and compound.

surfaces.label: Indoor concrete off-road floor
surfaces.note: Sealed or bare warehouse slab used as an indoor off-road base, sometimes lightly dirt-dressed; low-to-medium, smooth grip.

surfaces.label: Sand-dressed hockey-pitch astroturf
surfaces.note: Field-hockey artificial pitch (sand- or water-dressed nylon) reused for outdoor off-road; longer, abrasive pile, slick when wet.

surfaces.label: Sealed / painted asphalt
surfaces.note: Permanent track given a sealer/paint coat to smooth and stabilise grip; medium-high, more consistent than raw asphalt.

surfaces.label: Polished / worn-smooth asphalt
surfaces.note: Older, heavily-trafficked asphalt polished smooth; medium but slick, low mechanical key, additive-reliant for touring/pan cars.

surfaces.label: Rough / coarse-aggregate asphalt
surfaces.note: Coarse-chip asphalt and many parking-lot circuits; medium and abrasive — high grip but eats tyres fast, favours harder compounds.

surfaces.label: Parking-lot / car-park asphalt
surfaces.note: Temporary club-day layouts taped out on public car parks; dusty, unsealed, inconsistent low-to-medium grip grassroots racing.

surfaces.label: High-grip carpet (CRC black)
surfaces.note: Aggressive black competition carpet (e.g. CRC black) for 1:12 and pan-car nationals; very high, instant hook-up, traction-roll prone.

surfaces.label: Low-grip / loop carpet
surfaces.note: Club halls and older/loop-pile carpet with reduced traction; low-to-medium, easier on novices and lower-power classes.

surfaces.label: Micro / Mini-Z carpet
surfaces.note: Asia-standard surface for Mini-Z and 1/24-1/28 micro on-road (vs RCP foam in the US); low-pile carpet, high consistent grip.

surfaces.label: P-tile (polypropylene drift tile)
surfaces.note: The Japanese-standard competition RC drift surface (interlocking PP tiles); low, consistent slick-dry break-away, run with hard P-tile tires.

surfaces.label: RCP modular tile (drift / smooth side)
surfaces.note: Smooth face of RCP modular tiles for home/club drift; low-to-medium, slides predictably — flips to a groomed grip side.

surfaces.label: RCP modular tile (grip / groomed side)
surfaces.note: Groomed, lightly-textured face of RCP modular tiles for grip-style on-road and faster club drift; medium bite.

surfaces.label: Vinyl / PVC floor tile
surfaces.note: Vinyl/PVC click-floor or sheet vinyl as a drift surface; low-to-medium mid-tier slide, a budget alternative to P-tile.

surfaces.label: Smooth ceramic / porcelain tile
surfaces.note: Household glazed ceramic/porcelain floor tile used for impromptu drift; very low, hard and glassy, grout lines can grab.

surfaces.label: Painted / sealed MDF (hardboard)
surfaces.note: Sealed MDF/tempered hardboard sheets, the cheapest DIY drift surface; low slick-dry, humidity-sensitive, seams can catch tires.

surfaces.label: Drift carpet (CS-compound)
surfaces.note: Carpet used as a dedicated drift surface (Asia-standard alongside P-tile), run with hard CS/PE compound drift tires; medium, consistent.

surfaces.label: Wet / watered drift tile
surfaces.note: P-tile or smooth floor misted with water for low-grip deep-angle tandem comp drift; very low and glassy, changes tire choice dramatically.

surfaces.label: Raw asphalt (no-prep drag)
surfaces.note: Unprepared outdoor asphalt swept clean only — the dominant grassroots no-prep RC drag surface; low-to-medium, unpredictable bite.

surfaces.label: Prepped asphalt (VHT drag)
surfaces.note: Asphalt treated with VHT/PJ1-style traction compound and rubbered-in; high sticky bite for fastest 60-ft times.

surfaces.label: Raw concrete (no-prep drag)
surfaces.note: Unprepared bare concrete drag lane swept but not compounded; low-to-medium, bite varies with finish and dust.

surfaces.label: Prepped concrete (VHT drag)
surfaces.note: Concrete drag lane treated with VHT/PJ1-style traction compound and rubbered-in; high sticky launch-pad bite.

surfaces.label: Clay oval with cushion (berm)
surfaces.note: Loose material pushed up into a banked cushion against the wall on big outdoor clay ovals; high grip off the cushion, marbles below.

surfaces.label: Sealed / treated clay oval
surfaces.note: Clay bonded with a copolymer sealer (e.g. Soiltac) so it blue-grooves and grips like asphalt; premium high-grip ovals.

surfaces.label: High-banked clay oval
surfaces.note: Clay ovals with banked turns for higher corner speeds; sprint and late-model classes, grip varies with prep.

surfaces.label: Astroturf oval
surfaces.note: Outdoor astroturf RC ovals (popular UK/EU); medium-high grippy synthetic turf, consistent dry, slick wet — pan-car/on-road oval.

surfaces.label: Carpet oval (indoor)
surfaces.note: Indoor pan-car and on-road oval racing on low-pile carpet; high and very consistent, traction rolls possible.

surfaces.label: Natural rock / boulder field
surfaces.note: Outdoor comp rock crawling and scale trail on real boulders, ledges and rock gardens; high grip dry, slick when wet or dusty.

surfaces.label: Shale / loose scree slope
surfaces.note: Steep loose shale/scree faces on crawler trails and comp lines; low and loose — broken rock shifts underwheel.

surfaces.label: Concrete crawler comp course
surfaces.note: Permanent club/comp crawler courses built from poured concrete mountains and gated obstacles; high, consistent grip.

surfaces.label: Logs / roots / timber
surfaces.note: Fallen logs, exposed roots and timber crossings on scale trail and natural comp gates; dry bark grips, wet/mossy wood is slick.

surfaces.label: Water crossing / creek bed
surfaces.note: Stream/creek-bed crossings on scale trail and a standard water obstacle on club crawler courses; low, unpredictable, waterproof rigs required.

surfaces.label: Hard-packed dirt / fire road
surfaces.note: Compacted dirt fire-roads and packed rally/rallycross sections; medium-high clean, low and dusty when worn smooth.

surfaces.label: Tarmac / sealed rally stage
surfaces.note: Sealed asphalt rally and rallycross stage sections; high and abrasive, the paved high-grip end of the rally surface mix.

surfaces.label: Rallycross mixed (gravel + tarmac)
surfaces.note: Rallycross circuits combining sealed straights with gravel/dirt corners (incl. joker lap); split grip, needs compromise tires.

surfaces.label: Deep / fresh powder snow
surfaces.note: Fresh deep-snow scale bashing and snow-crawl events; very low — powder buries the chassis, needs tall paddle/snow tires or tracks.

surfaces.label: Smooth rink / sheet ice
surfaces.note: Polished sheet/rink ice for ice-drift and small-scale studded racing; extremely low and glassy, drift-prone even studded.

spring_systems.identification: Paint color on coil + length class (S/M/L); rate rises through the color chart; XGS part numbers for 1/8, IF/XGS for MP9/MP10
examples: 1/8 S-length: Gold = Medium (XGS003), Red = Medium Hard (XGS004), Yellow = Hard (XGS005), Orange = Super Hard (XGS006)
1/10 big bore: Green 9T 3.1 lb/in -> Grey 8T 3.6 -> Blue 7.5T 3.9 -> Yellow 7T 4.3 -> Red 6.5T 4.6 -> Orange 6T 5.1 lb/in

spring_systems.identification: Touring: 'C=' spring constant printed on package (4S springs, 20mm, hand-matched pairs); 1/8 offroad: number of paint dots (1-5) identifies rate, sets offered linear and progressive
examples: T4/X4 4S linear sets: C=2.1, C=2.3, C=2.6, C=3.0
4S progressive sets: C=2.3-2.6, C=2.5-2.8 (rate rises through stroke)
XB8 front 69mm progressive springs: 3-dot, 4-dot, 5-dot; rear 82mm: 2-dot etc.

spring_systems.identification: Paint color per spring family with rate in lb/in on AE's published spring rate charts (12mm, 13mm V2, 1/8 RC8 big bore)
examples: 13mm V2 buggy springs: color-coded (grey/blue/yellow/green/red/orange/white) spanning roughly 3-6 lb/in
RC8 1/8 springs listed by rate + color on AE 1/8 off-road spring list
Same color can mean different rates across families - always check the chart by spring series

spring_systems.identification: Rate in lb/in with color paint stripe; separate standard and Low Frequency (LF) spring lines (LF = softer initial feel for high-grip tracks)
examples: TLR 22-series 12mm springs by lb/in + color stripe
LF spring sets for carpet/astro high-bite conditions

spring_systems.identification: Linear springs = constant coil pitch, one rate through the stroke; progressive springs = variable pitch, rate increases with compression (soft initial, firm bottoming); identify by uneven coil spacing or dual-rate markings
examples: Progressive: predictable on bumpy outdoor tracks, resists bottoming
Linear: consistent feel preferred on smooth high-grip indoor tracks
Stiffer springs front = more on-power steering exit; stiffer rear = more steering into corner, less forward traction
